response.consequence: A request with optimized_pagination=true and a negative-offset cursor returns a 500 instead of a page. The 'advanced pagination' feature never works for the inputs it was written for.
response.explanation: When enable_advanced_features is set and cursor.offset < 0, get_result calls queryset[cursor.offset:stop] with a negative start. Django querysets do not support negative indexing and raise AssertionError ("Negative indexing is not supported."). The comment claiming the ORM handles negative slicing is wrong. The offset comes from the client-supplied cursor string. The audit log endpoint turns this path on for superusers and global-access members who pass optimized_pagination=true. For such a user, a cursor such as 100:-5:1 reaches this slice and fails. The stop value is also wrong: it is offset+limit+extra, which can be 0 or negative.

other_findings.consequence: A prev cursor with a negative offset still raises AssertionError and returns a 500 in every paginator that inherits from BasePaginator. Forward cursors with a negative offset now silently return the first page instead of failing.
other_findings.explanation: In BasePaginator.get_result, start_offset is max(0, offset) only when not cursor.is_prev. For is_prev cursors it stays equal to offset, so a negative offset is still sliced. This is the same unsupported negative slice as before. The added comment says negative offsets are handled, but only the non-prev case is clamped. The change to the shared base class has no benefit for existing callers. For non-prev cursors it silently changes an error into offset 0.
other_findings.title: BasePaginator now passes negative offsets through for prev cursors, contradicting its own comment

response.title: Negative-offset path slices the queryset with a negative start, which Django rejects
